findings.description: The bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so objects (including the uploaded vendor roster) are stored without enforced SSE-KMS/SSE-S3 encryption.
No ACL is set and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated, so bucket ACLs/policies could grant public access to report data with nothing blocking it.
The bucket contains business report data but has no logging block, so unauthorized access to objects cannot be detected or investigated.
Versioning is not enabled, so object overwrites or malicious/accidental deletions are unrecoverable; combined with force_destroy = true the data can be wiped without trace.
The ledger exports bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving sensitive financial export data unencrypted at rest.
No logging block is configured for this bucket, so reads/writes of ledger data are not recorded to an audit bucket.
Versioning is absent while force_destroy is true, so ledger export objects can be permanently destroyed or silently overwritten.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block guards this bucket, so a later ACL or bucket policy change could expose ledger data publicly.
The model artifacts bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so proprietary model data is stored without enforced encryption.
No public access block resource is attached, leaving the bucket open to accidental public exposure via ACL or policy changes.
Operational runbooks, which frequently contain sensitive procedures and infrastructure details, are stored without any server-side encryption configuration.
This bucket has no logging block, unlike model_artifacts and audit_trail, so access to runbook content is not auditable.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is defined for the runbooks bucket, so public access is not explicitly prevented at the account/bucket level.
The audit/log-delivery bucket itself has no logging configuration, so tampering with or exfiltration of collected audit logs would go unrecorded.
The bucket uses the log-delivery-write ACL but has no public access block, so the centralized log store is not protected against policy/ACL-based public exposure.
force_destroy = true on the audit log bucket allows all audit evidence to be deleted in a single terraform destroy, undermining the integrity of the audit trail.
A vendor roster spreadsheet (likely containing PII/business-sensitive data) is uploaded with no kms_key_id or server_side_encryption attribute, into a bucket that also lacks default encryption.
